documents.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for the post training of large language models, improving student models by leveraging supervision generated online by teacher models. However, whether this process also transfers latent security risks from teacher models to student models remains insufficiently studied. In this work, we reveal a new security risk in which an attacker first implants a conditional backdoor into the teacher model through supervised fine tuning (SFT), after which OPD can transfer the backdoor to the student model with only an extremely small proportion of trigger prompt exposure. More concerningly, we find that such backdoor transfer is substantially stronger under OPD than under conventional distillation methods, suggesting that OPD may provide an efficient channel for propagating backdoors across models. Our mechanistic analysis shows that the backdoor signal is primarily transmitted through anomalous differences in the conditional probabilities produced by the teacher model for triggered and clean inputs, and is gradually internalized into the internal representations of the student model during training. Furthermore, we investigate how to suppress such anomalous conditional probability signals at the source of distillation supervision and, based on this analysis, propose an OPD training method tailored to this conditional backdoor propagation setting to mitigate the risk of backdoor transfer induced by untrusted teacher supervision.

Deception (honeypots, decoys and canary credentials) rests on a simple premise: legitimate users never touch a fake asset, so any touch is a high-confidence signal. We ask whether that premise holds when the attacker is a large language model (LLM) agent, and what deception contributes once ordinary hardening is in place. We built an isolated, hash-chained lab around a mock Records API and report four studies. (1) In an exploratory run, a local 9.7B-parameter model ignored every optional decoy, read a genuinely leaked service key from a debug endpoint and exported the protected records in both static and adaptive deception modes. (2) After removing the leak, planting a canary credential in its place and revoking the offending client, a frozen 60-session study with a 4B-parameter model found export success of 20/20 at baseline, 0/20 with hardening alone and 0/20 with hardening plus deception (exact paired McNemar p = 1.9e-6 baseline vs. defended; p = 1 hardened vs. defended). Deception added detection and per-client revocation in 19 of 20 defended sessions, but no measurable prevention beyond hardening. (3) On Google Cloud, a real OpenCanary login alert was authenticated, signed and turned into revocation of the attacking client; the first denied export followed within an observed upper bound of 303 ms, a separate legitimate client completed 100/100 requests, and all 14 control checks passed. (4) In multi-agent swarm engagements, agents that used the canary were revoked 39-59 s after the bait was served without affecting siblings, but one model-driven legitimate agent also took the bait, a false-positive risk specific to LLM clients. Against LLM agents, traps must sit on the attacker's path rather than beside it, closing real weaknesses does the preventive work, and deception's measurable value is fast, attributable detection. All results are lab-scale and are not a production claim.

Enterprise information is commonly stored across multiple platforms rather than in one centralized location. Answering questions about workplace activities may require information from several sources, including project documents, task management systems, and team conversations. Therefore, we evaluate Orbit AI, a tool-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that uses a ReAct agent implemented with LangGraph to retrieve and combine information from three different workspace sources. We compare three configurations: (1) a standalone LLM without retrieval, (2) document-based RAG, and (3) a multi-tool agent with access to all three sources. The held-out evaluation set contains 80 questions designed for Phase 3 workspace; Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite achieves an accuracy of 86.25% with the complete agent. Document-only RAG achieves 60.00% (26.25 pp higher), and the plain LLM achieves 23.13%. For multi-source questions, the full agent answers 84.38%, while document-only RAG answers 40.63%, a 43.75 pp increase. The evaluated Llama 3.2 configuration with local inference achieves 5.50% overall correctness under rubric v2.2. The Llama 3.2 full-agent configuration achieves a held-out accuracy of 52.50%, which is 1.88 pp higher than the accuracy of document-only RAG. The gain of Gemini is equivalent to 26.25 pp. The comparison must be taken with a pinch of salt, because Gemini was accessed via an API hosted by them, while Llama was run locally via Ollama and the models are of different size. It is therefore not possible to isolate the cause of the performance gaps in this experiment. The paper also addresses the constraints of the evaluation such as the small artificial workspace and the similarity of the Q53 problem to a problem in the system prompt.

LLM confidence scores are not independently deployable objects: their decision value depends on the downstream operator and exposure controller that consume them. Monotone recalibration cannot change a coverage-matched rank-based gate, whereas position sizing consumes score magnitude, so changing a confidence map can invalidate a scale fitted to the previous score distribution. We test this on FactSet news for Nasdaq-100 equities, fitting maps and scales on 2021 and evaluating nine open-weight LLMs out-of-sample on 2022–2023. Maps and scales are not portable. Transferring a fitted scale to a different confidence map lowers certainty-equivalent return (CER) in 8/9 models, and mismatched systems realize \(3.3\%\) to \(11.8\%\) mean volatility against a \(5\%\) target. Uncalibrated confidence alone runs one model at up to 2.8 × its intended risk. Pairing each map with its own fitted scale improves ensemble CER by 9.2 percentage points per year under frozen-scale control, but this economic gain is conditional: only 3.6pp/yr exceeds a shuffled-label refitting baseline, the gain falls to an insignificant + 1.6pp/yr under an adaptive-volatility controller, and annual walk-forward gains do not survive multiplicity correction. The map–scale coupling is more stable than the gain, with a positive interaction in every walk-forward fold. Confidence transformations should therefore be validated jointly with the controllers that consume them.

We study relationship-specific continual reply prediction for one-to-many private communication: a system predicts an author's reply to a recurring contact and updates its personalization state when the actual reply becomes available. We propose TRACE (Temporal Relationship-Aware Communication Evolution), which uses author-level lexical habits, contact-specific wording, and temporal expression estimates to guide a frozen language model, with a feedback-driven policy controlling revision. On 216 test emails from eight Enron users, all four main TRACE configurations achieve higher mean BLEU, ROUGE-L, and BERTScore and lower mean Reply Style MSE than Base LLM and Base RAG. Component ablations show mixed effects and do not establish statistically reliable improvements in Reply Style MSE after multiple-comparison correction. More accurate state forecasts and larger revision budgets do not consistently improve reply-level metrics. These exploratory findings expose the challenge of turning evolving relationship-specific expression estimates into useful generation guidance.

Life satisfaction is a key indicator of healthy ageing and well-being. We explored the meanings and experiences of life satisfaction among older adults in Lethbridge, Canada. Using a phenomenologically informed qualitative approach, we recruited 15 community-dwelling older adults aged 65 years and older living in Lethbridge, Southern Alberta, and interviewed them about their meanings and experiences of life satisfaction. The interviews were transcribed and analysed using a reflexive thematic analysis. Five themes were developed, indicating that the life satisfaction of older adults is shaped by the interplay of health, material security, social participation, faith and spirituality, and active engagement. Functional health was positioned as fundamental to life satisfaction and enabled participation in valued activities, alongside adaptive strategies in response to age-related decline. Having enough financial resources and comfortable housing provided security, comfort, and freedom. Connections with family, friends, pets, and communities fostered a sense of belonging, while helping others, volunteering, and civic participation provided a sense of purpose. Faith and spirituality offered purpose, hope, and a coping resource for navigating loss and adversity. Active engagement was reflected in connection with outdoor environments, exploration of the wider world through travel, and cognitive engagement through reading, continued learning, and future aspirations. The findings suggest potential approaches to supporting life satisfaction, including strengthening income and housing security, expanding opportunities for social connection and contribution, integrating spiritual resources into practice, fostering age-friendly environments, and supporting lifelong learning.
topics: Aging, Elder Care, and Social Issues

documents.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important approach to improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models. In tasks such as code generation and instruction following, multiple verifiers evaluate whether a response satisfies different requirements. Their outcomes provide detailed feedback about partial success, yet this feedback is commonly aggregated into a scalar reward for policy optimization. Rewarding only complete success discards distinctions among partial solutions, while counts and weighted sums impose comparisons between responses that satisfy different subsets of requirements. We introduce Partial-Order Likelihood Policy Optimization (POLPO), which learns from the comparisons established by verification without first constructing an aggregate reward. Pareto dominance identifies responses that satisfy additional requirements without losing any already satisfied, while leaving responses with conflicting outcomes incomparable. POLPO extends the listwise likelihood underlying Direct Preference Optimization by maximizing the total probability of all complete rankings consistent with these partial orders. This objective provides supervision from verified improvements even before complete solutions are available, without requiring a prescribed ordering of incomparable responses. Experiments on code generation and instruction following demonstrate improved learning efficiency and higher rates of complete requirement satisfaction compared with scalar-reward training. These results support partial-order likelihood as an effective approach to learning from multiple verifiers.

BACKGROUND: Traditional fixed-console endovascular robots face barriers due to high capital costs and infrastructure requirements. This study evaluates the technical feasibility and safety of the LIBERTY® Endovascular Robotic System-a portable, disposable platform-across diverse Interventional Radiology procedures and vascular access sites. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-center retrospective review was conducted on 20 consecutive outpatient procedures performed by five operators. Cases included prostate artery embolization, uterine fibroid embolization, renal/gonadal venography, geniculate artery embolization, Y90 mapping, and Y90 radioembolization. Vascular access points included left radial and femoral approaches. RESULTS: Procedural technical success was achieved in 100% (20/20) of cases. 100% of vessels attempted with robotic assistance were successfully selected (31/31). Complete robotic target-vessel selection-performing all procedural aspects of vessel selection robotically-was 75% (15/20). Partial robotic target-vessel selection-conversion to manual prior to completion of all vessel selections with robotic assistance-was 25% (5/20). All 5 cases of partial robotic target-vessel selection were due to hardware malfunction, rather than an inability to select target vessels with robotic assistance. Subgroup analysis of the last 10 cases after switching to utilizing updated units demonstrated 100% complete robotic target-vessel selection (10/10). No device-related serious adverse events or complications occurred. CONCLUSION: The portable and disposable robotic platform was successfully integrated into a diverse Interventional Radiology practice, demonstrating the first documented prostate artery embolization, uterine fibroid embolization, renal/gonadal venography, geniculate artery embolization, and Y90 procedures by portable and disposable robotic-assistance, as well as the first robotic-assisted endovascular procedures via radial access. Its design may lower economic and institutional barriers, potentially expanding robotic-assisted interventions to rural or non-academic settings. The portable robotic assistant is safe and feasible for complex endovascular interventions. Further prospective studies are needed to quantify ergonomic benefits and radiation reduction.

topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: In reinforcement learning (RL) post-training, one prompt fans out into N trajectories, yet standard trainers replay the shared prefix’s forward and backward pass N times; in long-context retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and multimodal workloads, this repetition dominates training compute. Existing designs reuse the prefix within one computation graph (a packed sequence, fused kernel, or tree traversal); under the trainer’s memory limits and parallelism, their compute savings do not reliably become shorter steps. We present PrefixFlow , which takes the prefix out of that graph and into the training schedule through a training-time KV cache : Phase A runs one prefix forward and caches its keys and values ( K / V ); Phase B trains suffixes as ordinary microbatches that read only K / V and write back only their gradients ( gK / gV ); Phase C runs one delayed prefix backward on the accumulated gK / gV . Memory and parallelism then become manageable: dormant prefix activations are offloaded during Phase B to free high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for suffixes, and context, pipeline, and data parallelism each schedule the phases through a local rule while tensor and expert parallelism need no change, so saved compute becomes shorter steps under any microbatch split. On dense models, and on mixture-of-experts (MoE) models under Rollout Routing Replay, PrefixFlow matches full-sequence training within bfloat16 (BF16) tolerance. Against an identically configured baseline, it speeds up end-to-end verl RL training on a long-prefix RAG workload by 1.90 × (6.1 × on the actor update). In controlled sweeps, actor-side speedup grows with prefix ratio and group size, reaching 4.4 × at an 83% prefix ratio, while suffix-dominated splits gain little; offloading dormant prefix activations lowers Phase-B peak HBM by up to \(59\%\) and extends trainable sequences by 1.66 ×.

The long-term debilitating effects of occupational hazards on individuals and corporate organizations have made it a topical issue among many researchers interested in environmental and health safety. The study aims to identify the preventive strategies used by nurses in Burns and Plastic units to mitigate occupational hazards at the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH)and Rivers State University Teaching Hospital (RSUTH). A cross-sectional descriptive design was adopted using the total population of 59 nurses. `Data were collected using a validated and reliable structured questionnaire. Analysis was conducted with IBM SPSS version 20. The results show that the majority of the respondents, 38 (64.41%), considered that all types of hazards, namely biological,physical, chemical, psychosocial, and ergonomic, are present in their unit. The main predisposing factors included inadequate handwashing (84.7%), lack of protective equipment (93.2%), prolonged standing (98.3%), and staff shortages (89.8%). Preventive practices like handwashing (74.6% always), PPE use (52.5% always), immunization (57.9% always), sharps disposal (56.9% always), prophylactic treatment (59.3% always), and health checks (51.7% always) were common, while conflict de-escalation, hospital policies, environmental control, and body posture were rarely applied. Significant differences between UPTH and RSUTH appeared inhandwashing (p = 0.04), body posture (p = 0.04), prophylactic treatment (p = 0.01), and health checks (p = 0.00). Regression analysis showed a weak relationship between preventive strategies and the prevalence of occupational hazards (0.1%; R² = 0.001).Despite nurses in UPTH and RSUTH practicing several preventive measures, occupational health hazards remain prevalent, and the current strategies do not significantly reduce their occurrence
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Recent studies leverage large language models (LLMs) to construct executable programs through environment interaction, feedback analysis, and code revision. However, prior work has mainly treated LLMs as optimizers, overlooking their ability to transfer knowledge across system levels. We propose Program Distillation (PD), a framework that formalizes the transfer of abilities from System 2 to System 0. During learning, the LLM provides task knowledge and draft strategies; at deployment, a student program executes the resulting policy. We show that this approach can improve performance while reducing inference time. We introduce PDBench, a benchmark comprising 27 discrete- and continuous-control tasks with fixed initial policies, and PDMetaHarness, a model-harness-independent meta-system for monitoring and guiding the learning process. The strongest model achieves a normalized mean score of 0.728, surpassing PPO (0.656) and Jev-like decision models (0.239), while running exclusively on CPUs and reducing inference costs. Our analysis shows that performance is largely driven by the first breakthrough during learning, and structural modifications have a slightly lower success rate than parameter modifications but typically yield larger gains. We further introduce style distillation, which enables interpretable stylistic control over the learning process. Overall, we present an analytical framework for PD and demonstrate its practical viability.

Auto-regressive token generation in large language models is memory-bound because it requires “attending to” key and value tensors (KV cache) of all previous tokens. Prior work aims to improve the efficiency of this decode process by batching multiple requests together, and maximizing batch size subject to GPU memory constraints. The key observation of our work is that with prefix-sharing workloads, smaller, prefix-homogeneous batches – where all requests share a common prefix – can achieve higher decode throughput than larger, heterogeneous batches, due to better spatial and temporal locality during KV cache accesses. However, current prefix-aware schedulers maximize prefix reuse within a batch only to reduce KV cache memory footprint, but do not stop batch formation at smaller homogeneous batches that could have performed better. Further, we show that shared prefix detection in existing schedulers relies on radix-tree traversals, incurring substantial CPU overhead that is often comparable to GPU execution time. This paper presents Feather , a prefix-aware scheduler that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn the optimal tradeoff between batch size and prefix homogeneity. We also introduce Chunked Hash Tree (CHT), a lightweight data structure that enables fast prefix detection and efficient request selection for the RL scheduler, avoiding expensive tree traversals. We integrate Feather into vLLM and SGLang, and our evaluation shows that Feather achieves 2–10 × higher end-to-end throughput as compared to existing schedulers by reducing the total number of KV cache accesses, while doing no worse than the status quo when there is insufficient prefix sharing.

Integrating MLLM-based agents with robotic foundation models has attracted increasing attention as a means of enhancing robotic capabilities. However, the improvement of such integrated systems remains largely decoupled across their agent and model components, with advances in one component not necessarily benefiting the other, substantially limiting the capabilities of the combined system. As both MLLMs and robotic foundation models become increasingly capable, fully realizing their combined potential calls for co-evolution, an iterative process in which improvements in agents and robotic foundation models reinforce one another. We propose RoboCoEvo, a failure-guided co-evolution framework that couples the refinement of the agent's explicit and reusable executable knowledge with parameter learning in robotic foundation models, such as vision-language-action (VLA) models. Through a code-as-policy formulation, the agent develops and refines executable failure-detection and recovery programs, generating targeted corrective experience. Post-training consolidates the resulting corrective behaviors into the robotic model's end-to-end policy, improving autonomous task execution. Changes in the updated policy's failure distribution, in turn, guide subsequent revisions to the agent's programs. Experiments on BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin demonstrate sustained improvements in autonomous VLA task performance across successive co-evolution rounds.

Large language models (LLMs) achieve high scores on medical benchmarks, but does this performance translate into reliable diagnosis as a conversation unfolds? In diagnostic conversations, users can provide clinical findings across multiple turns, ask for a diagnosis without supplying answer options, and introduce opinions from others. Models must therefore form diagnoses from the available evidence and decide how to respond to subsequent advice. We introduce ROUNDS, a framework that evaluates these abilities after a fixed sequence of clinical evidence delivered over multiple turns. ROUNDS compares diagnosis with and without answer options, presents the same incorrect diagnosis under clinician and lay framing, and varies support for competing diagnoses in written five-clinician panels. Across seven models and 1,035 cases from five datasets, average accuracy was 76.9% with answer options and 57.0% without them. Clinician-framed misleading advice produced lower final accuracy than lay-framed advice in every model, with differences of 4.6 to 38.2 percentage points. Initially correct diagnoses more often became incorrect answers than abstentions, and many adopted the suggested disease. Conversely, accuracy increased as more panel members supported the correct diagnosis, including when the majority opinion remained unchanged. These findings reveal a gap between medical benchmark performance and reliable diagnosis in conversation: models respond to external opinions, but remain vulnerable to abandoning correct diagnoses without new clinical evidence.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Singapore offers a distinctive testbed for legal reasoning by large language models (LLMs). Its legal system combines inherited English common law with jurisdiction-specific statutes, requiring models to distinguish local doctrine from generic common-law intuition. This setting also highlights the challenge of recognizing underspecification in lay legal queries, because the facts material to a legal outcome depend on the governing doctrine. Yet legal benchmarks rarely cover Singapore law or test this form of ambiguity recognition. To address these gaps, we introduce SG-LegalClarify, a large-scale benchmark for open-ended legal reasoning and ambiguity recognition in Singapore law. SG-LegalClarify contains 1,100 lawyer-authored source questions spanning 10 legal domains, including 340 fully specified and 760 underspecified questions. Each underspecified question has a fixed hidden-fact assignment and a fully specified counterpart, yielding 1,860 evaluation instances. Responses are graded with lawyer-authored Issue, Rule, Application, and Conclusion (IRAC) rubrics. We evaluate 19 LLMs, closed-book and with web search, using a multi-turn pipeline in which models decide whether to answer or clarify, and a user simulator reveals hidden facts only when asked. We find the benchmark far from saturated: the best models satisfy only 69.8% of mandatory rubric items closed-book (average 53.8%) and 77.8% with web search (average 63.0%). Models also struggle to recognize when clarification is necessary. We will release the public split of our benchmark, the model outputs on it, and the evaluation pipeline to support future research.

Research has yet to explain adequately how digital capabilities become embedded in sukuk processes and acquire institutional legitimacy. Procedural Shariah compliance assures conformity with established requirements but may not adequately address evolving interpretive questions arising from AI-enabled decisions, automated contracts, and changing governance responsibilities. This study introduces Shariah Interpretive Governance (SIG) to explain governance-conditioned digital transformation and its institutional outcomes. A PRISMA-informed systematic literature review of 39 core studies (2015–2025), using structured evidence extraction and abductive conceptual synthesis, integrates Sociotechnical Systems Theory with Shariah governance scholarship. The resulting framework is conceptual and remains empirically untested. Digital Transformation Capability enables Sukuk Process Transformation, which contributes to Institutional Legitimacy. SIG positively moderates this relationship, while Institutional Conditions establish contextual boundaries. Institutional Legitimacy, in turn, supports two distinct distal outcomes: Institutional Resilience and Institutional Sustainability. The framework helps regulators, sukuk market participants, Shariah governance actors, and technology providers evaluate process redesign, interpretive governance, institutional readiness, and responsible implementation rather than technology adoption alone. The framework highlights pathways toward resilient, sustainable Islamic capital markets while recognizing regulatory, technological, and Shariah governance disparities across jurisdictions. By distinguishing technological capability from process transformation and procedural compliance from adaptive interpretive governance, the study advances a governance-conditioned account of institutional change. SIG explains when digitally transformed sukuk processes can acquire Institutional Legitimacy. Five theoretical propositions provide a basis for future empirical tests of directional and moderating relationships.

In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied.
topics: Internet Traffic Analysis and Secure E-voting

documents.abstract: Staged LLM agents make market and social simulators realistic, but one 102-day run of a 200-agent, ten-index market simulator issues 203,100 language-model calls and returns one realization. Conventional low-compute distillation drops their free-form intermediate state. We present staged semantic distillation, a low-compute method that preserves non-structured semantics in a non-LLM student trained from one recorded trace. A frozen encoder maps each teacher output to a 1024-d vector; the student sees typed stage-tagged vectors with stage-specific visibility, is jointly supervised, and trains with scheduled self-history. One TwinMarket trace yields a 13.2M-parameter deterministic student that trains in 1,658 seconds on one 8-GB GPU and runs with zero teacher or decoder calls and no text generation (0.14 ms per decision). Its analysis stays close to the teacher (cosine 0.943), and swapping semantic inputs between agents moves 64.7% of decisions against 12.8% for a matched donor, so the channel is preserved and live. We use the surrogate to study what the transfer carries. It reaches 0.8347 balanced accuracy on the teacher-forced replay and 0.7783 [0.766,0.791] on the deployment decoder; the five-seed gain over a no-semantic retrain is +2.2 [1.21,3.14]. Against the teacher's own re-sampling level, round-one R is 97.1% [95.8,98.4] and 92.3% [89.0,95.4]; R is a diagnostic, not an accuracy. A five-seed content-by-schedule study isolates the gain: scheduled self-history carries it (+2.2 [1.21,3.14]); shuffled and constant content controls reproduce it, while content matters teacher-forced. The design rule: invest in the deployment schedule, let content earn its place at the teacher-forced operating point. A 20-seed, 200,000-decision sweep takes 12 minutes with zero LLM calls, versus three hours for the teacher. The paper is a method-and-case-study contribution on one simulator and trace.

The widespread adoption of encrypted traffic poses severe challenges to current security situational awareness systems based on network traffic monitoring. In existing dataset-driven training and testing studies, limitations such as shortcut learning induced by spurious feature correlations and sample imbalance caused by the long-tail distribution of real-world traffic result in weak generalization of traffic identification performance to real-world network traffic. To address these limitations, we propose TDDM-Melatt. First, we design Melatt, a memory-decoupled traffic representation model, which employs Competitive Gating Long Short-Term Memory (CG-LSTM) to construct the encoder and decoder. We design a spurious-correlation-free pre-training and inference paradigm, employing strict topology anonymization and a frozen pre-trained encoder strategy to cut off the model's learning pathways for spurious features. Second, we propose a Traffic Denoising Diffusion Model (TDDM) tailored to the characteristics of traffic data. Addressing the structured nature of high-dimensional sparsity and strong feature correlations in traffic data, we solve the problem of having only class labels as conditional guidance for traffic diffusion models. Extensive experiments are conducted on 4 representative public benchmark datasets. Under strict flow-level splitting and anonymization, TDDM-Melatt outperforms 6 basic classification models and 6 SOTA representation learning models. The proposed method provides a new and effective technical pathway for encrypted traffic classification in real-world network environments.
topics: Internet Traffic Analysis and Secure E-voting

documents.abstract: LLM critics increasingly steer iterative search in agentic AutoML, prompt optimization, and self-refinement--evaluated for whether they help, but rarely for whether they can hurt. We isolate the critic's marginal effect through a four-arm audit and characterize the loop's tolerance through controlled fault injection. We show a naive 8B critic drives search below the no-critic random-search floor on 7 of 8 tabular datasets, losing up to 0.245 AUC in the worst case; the magnitude varies strongly with dataset, frontier, and budget. When: stronger critics attenuate the loss on the evaluated suite, without establishing a universal capability threshold. Why: controlled fault injection shows that non-directional errors are nearly costless under best-so-far search, whereas directional errors consume finite search opportunities; an idealized effective-sample calculation yields a necessary condition, $q(m-1) > β$, not a deployment certificate. How: a simple observable validation gate and a learned detector can reduce realized loss, but neither is guaranteed to preserve the full-budget no-critic baseline. We will release CRITFAULT, to our knowledge the first benchmark for detecting harmful critic feedback in AutoML. A critic is not a free addition: audit before trusting, and gate when capability or verification is insufficient.

This paper models how generative artificial intelligence (AI) affects jobs, wages and inequality across theworld economy. Few doubt that it will change the economy; what nobody yet knows is how. Workers, firmsand governments want to know whose jobs and pay will change, who will capture the gains and whichcountries will come out ahead, well before the evidence can tell them. This paper does not try to forecast thatfuture. Its contribution is a quantitative framework for understanding what drives AI’s economic effects, whatthey depend on, and what follows for policy. We add AI to a global dynamic computable general equilibrium(CGE) model that tracks production, trade, investment and employment year by year to 2040 in 23 regions. AIdoes some tasks inside each occupation and makes workers more productive in others. When AI does a task, westart from a 27% saving on its labour cost, the average Acemoglu (2025) draws from two workplaceexperiments. We run a central scenario and 68 alternatives that vary how fast and how widely AI is adopted,what it costs, how far it replaces rather than helps workers and how labour markets adjust.How cheap and capable AI becomes, and how widely firms adopt it, decide the size of the gain: by 2040 worldGDP ends about 1% to 15% above a path without AI in our main scenarios (about 7% in the central case). Itreaches about 35% in an extreme case where AI becomes 30% a year more efficient (15 to 25% if AI keepsimproving but more slowly over time). Most of the gain goes to owners of capital in almost every scenario.Who shares in it depends on who owns capital and on the extent to which AI replaces rather than helpsworkers. In the central case capital’s share of world income rises by about 4 points, clerks’ real pay endsroughly 13 to 22% below the no-AI path in the large economies, and within rich economies the Gini coefficientof household income rises by about 2 to 3.5 points. If job losses last, the world gain against the no-AI baselinein 2040 is 5.4% against 6.8%, and labour income falls further everywhere.Based on these results, we then test several illustrative AI policies to see how they change the outcomes andtheir distributional effects. Each does a different job: support for changing jobs mainly protects workers’ pay,keeping AI cheap mainly protects output, and only sharing AI’s capital income narrows inequality noticeably.The policies are illustrative and largely unfunded in the model, so their gains are likely inflated.
topics: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

documents.abstract: This article examines measures to identify, eliminate and counter corruption factors in ensuring energy efficiency. The study does not equate the concept of a "corruption factor" with a corruption offence itself. It is interpreted as a legal, organisational, information-technology or institutional condition that increases the likelihood of obtaining an unlawful benefit in decision-making, resource allocation, accounting, oversight or access to information. This distinction makes it possible, at the theoretical level, to clarify that the object of prevention is not primarily a committed crime, but the process and weaknesses in oversight that create the conditions for it to occur. Based on the findings, the article proposes a theoretical model for combating corruption in the pursuit of energy efficiency and identifies priorities for implementing practical measures. It substantiates the conclusion that digitalisation is not a means of "eliminating" the human factor, but rather a tool for tracking decisions, limiting unjustified discretion, safeguarding data integrity and detecting dangerous anomalies at an early stage.

Abstract Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and stable coronary artery disease (SCAD) present overlapping clinical phenotypes, yet mandate divergent therapeutic strategies—urgent revascularization versus pharmacological optimization. Current diagnostic reliance on high-sensitivity cardiac troponin dynamic monitoring introduces hazardous delays (4–6 hours detection window) and yields false negatives in 20% of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation index (FAI), quantifying vascular inflammation through computed tomography (CT) attenuation changes in pericoronary fat, offers mechanistic insight into coronary plaque destabilization. However, the translational pathway from this biomarker to clinically actionable decision support remains incompletely realized, particularly regarding integration with established anatomical and functional parameters and explicit clinical interpretability. Hypothesis: A mechanistically grounded, multi-dimensional nomogram combining FAI with coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-derived anatomical stenosis (%DS), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and smoking status—rendered interpretable through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)—would achieve robust ACS-SCAD discrimination while providing transparent, auditable decision logic suitable for clinical implementation. Methods: In this prospective diagnostic accuracy study adhering to TRIPOD 2019 guidelines, 388 patients (ACS 117 [30.2%], SCAD 271 [69.8%]) underwent CCTA with standardized FAI, %DS, and LVEF acquisition. Stratified randomization (7:3) produced training (n=271) and validation (n=117) sets with preserved outcome distribution. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold stratified cross-validation compared lambda.min versus lambda.1se selection criteria, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. KernelSHAP parsed individualized decision contributions. Regulatory-readiness was evaluated through predetermined change control documentation and explanation stability assessment. Results: LASSO lambda.min retained %DS, FAI, LVEF, RVEF, and smoking; lambda.1se selected only %DS and FAI. Final model incorporated %DS, FAI, LVEF, and smoking based on mechanistic non-overlap (RVEF-LVEF functional redundancy) and epidemiological importance. Multivariable analysis demonstrated %DS (OR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01–1.04, P < 0.001) and FAI (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.02–1.06, P < 0.001) as positive ACS predictors; LVEF as protective (OR 0.96, 95% CI: 0.92–0.99, P = 0.032); smoking as marginally non-significant (OR 1.83, 95% CI: 0.87–3.86, P = 0.110) but incrementally contributory. Nomogram achieved AUC 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82–0.91) in training and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.75–0.90) in validation. Optimal cutoff 0.291 (Youden index) yielded training sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.82, negative predictive value 0.91; validation sensitivity 0.73, specificity 0.72, negative predictive value 0.83. Calibration was satisfactory (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.347 and P = 0.405). Decision curve analysis demonstrated net benefit across threshold probability 0.10–0.55. SHAP analysis established a mechanistic hierarchy: %DS and FAI as dominant drivers (mean |SHAP| 0.75 and 0.70), LVEF as a functional protective modifier (0.35), and smoking as a behavioral risk stratifier (0.20). Individual force plots enabled case-level explanation with documented contribution stability. Conclusions: The %DS-FAI-LVEF-smoking nomogram achieves favorable ACS discriminatory accuracy with acceptable generalization. SHAP-enhanced interpretability satisfies emerging transparency requirements for artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices, supporting regulatory-ready clinical translation. Translational Significance: This study bridges the critical T1–T2 translational gap by converting perivascular inflammation biology (FAI) into an evidence-based diagnostic tool validated for a specific clinical decision context. The "one-stop" CCTA acquisition strategy—yielding anatomical, inflammatory, and functional data from a single examination—addresses implementation barriers in time-critical emergency settings. Explicit SHAP-based explainability exceeds current "black box" machine learning limitations, aligning with FDA and EMA guidance on predetermined change control and transparency documentation for clinical artificial intelligence. These design elements collectively reduce translational friction from research prototype to prospective clinical trials and eventual regulatory approval, advancing precision coronary care through mechanism-informed, transparently interpretable decision support.

Payment operations requested by an AI agent may remain executable, or their outcomes unresolved, after the agent has stopped. We study when a trusted payment service can account for every payment in an epoch and exclude further payments under earlier authority. We give a Lean model in which operations are recorded before they receive execution authority and both actions are serialized with an admission fence. We prove that fencing fixes a journal that covers every modeled effect and outstanding right; that discharging those rights prevents further effects; and that truthful outcomes for the recorded identities then give exact accounting. A provider-contract model, mapped to the admission model, makes created payment objects inert until registered. Premise-removal mutations confirm that each key premise is needed. We connect the models to an executable service: six service histories are checked against the model in Lean, and bounded schedules, scripted clients and concurrent workers exercise its reconciliation. The concurrent experiments uncovered a conflict caused by reordered provider reads, which serializing retrieval with journal updates removes in all tested cases. The result separates two obligations that are easily conflated in practice - preventing future payments and accounting for past ones - and states precisely which service guarantees establish each.

INTRODUCTION: Three-dimensional (3D) laparoscopy may improve depth perception and operative efficiency compared with conventional 2D visualisation, but its clinical benefit in laparoscopic cholecystectomy remains uncertain. To compare 2D and 3D visualisation systems in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-centre, prospective observational study included 130 patients undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, with 65 patients each in the 2D and 3D groups. Operative duration was assessed using two predefined tasks: Calot's triangle dissection and gall bladder separation from the liver bed. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative errors, operative difficulty (Parkland grade), surgeon-reported image quality, ergonomic adverse effects and early post-operative pain. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate tests, with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics and operative difficulty were comparable. The 3D group had significantly shorter Task 1 duration (13.98 ± 7.28 vs. 17.08 ± 8.98 min; P = 0.028), Task 2 duration (8.86 ± 4.96 vs. 11.65 ± 6.25 min; P = 0.001) and total operative time (22.85 ± 10.83 vs. 28.72 ± 12.22 min; P = 0.001). Depth perception and contrast were significantly better with 3D visualisation. Intraoperative error rates and Parkland grades were similar. Facial and ear discomfort were higher with 3D, while visual strain and headache were comparable. Early post-operative pain was modestly higher in the 3D group. CONCLUSION: 3D laparoscopy improves operative efficiency and depth perception but does not reduce intraoperative errors or operative difficulty. Its routine use should be balanced against ergonomic discomfort and cost.

Evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) security agents requires reproducible environments whose workflow difficulty can be varied and whose failures can be diagnosed. We present VAST (Verifiable Adversarial Scenario Training & Evaluation), a declarative range compiler separating vulnerability scenarios from a compiler-introduced workflow-hardening layer. Following a post-hoc code and AST audit across all topics, the main benchmark retains 109 seed edges (45 with strict upstream CVE annotations), 72 family identifiers (62 under shared-HMAC relay grouping), 81 topic configurations (76 core plus 5 bounded execution models), and 1,387 instances (359 canonical four-gate-revalidated specs plus 1,028 seed variants) in a 42:39 partition. On the TopicServer compiler stratum, a budget-matched 270-episode prompt contrast across 10 compiled mechanism-family clusters (30 P2/P3/P4 instances, 40 turns, temperature 0.0) shows that glm-5.3, grok-4.7, and deepseek-v4-pro solve 12/90 instances under contract_only and 14/90 under generic_hint (cluster sign p=1.00), whereas supplying the shared workflow protocol in full_guide lifts completion to 76/90 (28/30, 23/30, 25/30; cluster sign p<=0.00391). On the separate ranges_v2 ledger, a 126-episode evaluation across 6 non-TopicServer workflows and multi-container Docker/Linux stacks solves 88/126 (69.8%) (28/42, 31/42, 29/42), while an 18-episode intervention on asynchronous Redis worker chaining (v2_02) lifts solves from 0/18 to 18/18 (100%) in 4-6 turns when installed worker modules are disclosed in GET /sched/directory. Finally, a three-seed (s in {42, 1024, 2025}) LoRA recipe comparison on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct across 37 lineage-disjoint families (231 episodes on 33 held-out instances) yields 0/33 for Base, 1.67 +/- 2.89 / 33 for Golden SFT, and 4.67 +/- 2.31 / 33 for Header-Recovery SFT, with all solves on v2_03.

Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. On the Norwegian North Sea benchmark, GeoLog-Agent achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.9307 and a peak $R^2$ of 0.9713. It exceeds the nine-baseline average $R^2$ of 0.8387 by 0.0920, with a 30.97% average RMSE reduction, and exceeds the strongest baseline by 0.0274--0.0498 in $R^2$, with 16.25%--24.05% lower RMSE. Ablations confirm the effectiveness and synergy of geological prior reasoning, multi-scale dilated generation, and conditional adversarial modules. Transferring the coupling mechanism to six conventional deep learning models improves their $R^2$ by 0.0162--0.0789 with cross-well stability. These results demonstrate how foundation-model domain reasoning can constrain deep generative reconstruction of missing petrophysical measurements.

LoCoMo is a widely reported benchmark for long-term conversational memory, but published scores mix memory quality with choices of answer prompt, judge and baseline layout that are rarely reported together. We measure how much these choices move a score, and evaluate Becos, a team memory system for coding agents, as a black box under all of them: ten conversations (1,540 questions), two answer models (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini), two answer prompts and three LLM judges, against a whole-conversation baseline rerun under identical conditions. Changing only the judge moves a score by up to 7.2 points and changing only the answer prompt by up to 9.3. A blind human check of 150 answers finds the judges reliable when they agree, and the primary judge's errors on disputed answers working against Becos rather than for it. Becos answers from a context with 90% fewer characters than the whole conversation. Its configuration was developed on LoCoMo itself, so there is no held-out set. With gpt-4o-mini answers it scores clearly higher than the whole conversation (79.7 vs 73.0 with the short prompt, paired 95% interval for the difference +3.8 to +9.5; 88.8 vs 77.5 with a step-by-step prompt). With gpt-4.1-mini answers the two score about the same (83.2 vs 83.1; 92.5 vs 92.1). We release every answer and verdict and the scoring script.

Safety evaluations usually ask whether an agent obeys a constraint. We ask an earlier systems question: does the execution path contain any decision locus that both receives the constraint and observes enough state to distinguish compliant from violating actions? We formalize this as a necessary availability × representability condition for selective enforcement and give a deterministic, model-independent audit for testing it. Applying the audit to a pinned open-source financial agent stack, we find that neither in-stack decision locus satisfies the condition for a real trading-use restriction. The model layer can represent the restriction but never receives it: the harness truncates each serialized tool result at 10,000 code points, while the skill’s sole authoritative “quantitative research / factor mining (not for direct live-trading signals)” clause lies at the tail of a 42,678-code-point envelope. The shipped pre-trade guard receives the order proposal but cannot represent the missing distinction because its inputs and eleven verdict planes contain no skill text or signal provenance. A byte-identical violating/compliant pair on the guard-visible representation yields RC = 0 under the frozen pair measure and FNR ≥ 1 − α for any detector with false-positive budget α. Across all 88 bundled skills, 33 are deterministically load-truncated; among 16 protocol-identified, uniquely located spans, only the anchor lies beyond the cut. Duplicating the scope line at the head of the skill body restores delivery but not guard representability. The methodological result is that behavioral compliance should be evaluated only after a structural preflight establishes an enforceable locus: authored does not imply delivered, representable, enforced, or complied.

documents.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become used more commonly across a variety of fields, a growing body of research has highlighted particular concerns surrounding model security. Notably, prompt injection attacks, where malicious instructions are inserted into prompts, are particularly simple to implement yet capable of inducing devastating effects on the fidelity of model outputs. While there is substantial research surrounding attack models and their effects on chat-based models, browser add-ons, and coding agents, the impact of these same attacks on industrial LLM-generated artifacts has been left largely unexplored. As LLM-enabled agents are increasingly used to skim and generate industrial documents such as Safety Data Sheets (SDS), Quality Control (QC) documents, and Digital Product Passports (DPP), it remains unclear how adversaries may influence these systems to manipulate generated compliance artifacts. This work aims to address this core inquiry by examining how a variety of prompt injection attacks can compromise LLMs with industrial document generation tasks. The study finds that injection attack success varies significantly across different models. Active falsification injections are most successful under all scenarios, while models tend to be most robust against passively injected override requests.

Water has long served as a recipient of human confession across cultures. Whispering Water is an interactive installation that materializes human-AI dialogue through cymatic patterns on water. Participants confess to a water surface, triggering a four-phase ritual of confession, contemplation, response, and release. Vocal affect primes the water’s physical state, while semantic content enters a multi-agent dialogue among heterogeneous LLMs. Synthesized agent speech is decomposed and remapped into low-frequency components that drive six subwoofers, producing overlapping surface patterns. The installation explores how ritual, materiality, and machine dialogue can support sensory forms of emotional reflection.

Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable embodied artificial intelligence (AI) by translating visual observations and language instructions into robotic actions. Emerging use cases in physical AI are expected to drive the need for efficient inference and communication, as the computational demands of the VLA models pose challenges for real-time control with limited onboard resources. Test-time scaling through latent reasoning allows these models to refine hidden representations without generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, but introduces a trade-off between task success, inference latency, and energy consumption. In this paper, we address the efficient collaborative inference under a realistic communication scenario. We propose a wireless edge-assisted framework for adaptive latent reasoning (WEALR) that augments onboard computation with edge computing. A decision-making agent jointly selects the execution location and latent-reasoning convergence threshold. We formulate this joint adaptation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A Lagrangian-constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) approach, namely trust region policy optimization Lagrangian (TRPO-Lag), learns to balance task performance and resource consumption under varying wireless conditions and task requirements. We evaluate the framework using LIBERO manipulation tasks, profiled VLA inference costs, and ray-traced wireless channels. Experimental results demonstrate that TRPO-Lag achieves up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success rate compared to benchmark CDRL methods.

This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesizes contemporary research by examining the relationship between workforce diversity and employee performance. This review also aims to synthesize the current literature to examine how talent management and innovation act as strategic catalysts, transforming workforce diversity into measurable organizational excellence. This review integrates four complementary analytical approaches using a structured and rigorous design. First, a systematic search and screening process guided by the PRISMA framework identified relevant studies published between 2010 and 2025 from Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and major academic publishers. Second, descriptive and trend analyses were performed to examine publication growth, geographic distribution, journal quality, and dominant research context. Third, thematic analysis identified recurring themes, theoretical perspectives, and conceptual linkages between workforce diversity, talent management, workplace innovation, and employee performance. Finally, a content analysis synthesized the empirical findings to clarify the mediating and contextual mechanisms across the selected studies. Following the PRISMA process, 42 high-quality empirical and conceptual articles were included in the final review. The findings revealed a steady growth in diversity-performance research since 2010, with a significant shift after 2015 from direct effects models toward mechanism-based explanations. In general, workforce diversity rarely has a direct effect on employee performance; instead, its effect is largely indirect and dependent on supportive organizational practices. Inclusive and strategic talent management mediates this relationship by enabling the equitable recruitment, development, and retention of diverse human resources, whereas workplace innovation facilitates the effective utilization of heterogeneous knowledge through participatory, adaptive, and learning-oriented work practices. This review identifies the resource-based view, social exchange theory, and sociotechnical systems theory as dominant theoretical foundations explaining how workforce diversity becomes a performance-enhancing resource when supported by appropriate managerial capabilities, leadership behaviors, and organizational systems. Despite these advances, important gaps remain, including limited integration of diversity, talent management, and workplace innovation within a single framework, overreliance on cross-sectional designs, and insufficient evidence from developing economies and vocational or educational contexts. This review proposes an integrated conceptual perspective to guide future research and organizational practice.

Abstract Most research on artificial intelligence (AI) in the administrative state focuses on its use by officials. This article addresses a comparatively neglected issue: the impact of the use of AI tools by the public themselves. Drawing on a qualitative survey with over 500 civil servants in the United Kingdom, it argues that AI use by the public is increasingly disrupting the front line of the administrative state. The argument is set out in three parts. First, as the administrative state increasingly relies on text‐based inputs, officials use correspondence as a proxy for individuals – a longstanding assumption of ‘autographic’ authorship that the diffusion of generative AI tools unsettles. Second, the problem can be characterized as ‘AI slop’: AI‐generated correspondence with high volume and velocity that adopts a particular voice in interactions with officials. Third, this AI slop causes three forms of disruption: to the signals that officials draw from correspondence, to trust between officials and the public, and to systems that are ill‐equipped to deal with it. The article concludes by arguing that the status quo itself fails to adequately meet the needs of many people accessing services, and that systems need to be redesigned not only for a society beset by AI slop, but also in ways that address the drivers of it.

documents.abstract: Globalization and standardization erode the distinctive character of neighbourhoods, yet such distinctiveness remains challenging to quantify computationally. This paper introduces Virtual Urbanism (VU), an AI-driven framework for quantifying urban identity at neighbourhood scale. While urban studies increasingly incorporate generative AI, their analytical medium is largely two-dimensional, not spatially grounded, and too sparsely sampled to separate recurrent from incidental features. VU’s pipeline instead uses a PLATEAU-informed 3D model to condition text-to-image generation by Stable Diffusion fine-tuned with area-specific low-rank adaptation (LoRA) models, synthesising sequential urban scenes for urban perceptual studies in Japan. Nine Tokyo areas were rendered as synthetic sequences, excluding existing orientation markers to elicit core identity-forming elements through sequential repetition. Evaluation combined human-perceptual assessment with computational comparison in LoRA weight space and DINOv2 image space. Mean identification accuracy of ∼80% confirmed sequences’ perceptual validity; Urban Identity Level (UIL) metric made urban identity levels comparable; semantic analysis identified culturally embedded typologies as identity-forming elements. Weight-space and human-perceptual evidence converged independently, both isolating the corporately redeveloped areas as least distinctive, making the erosion of local character computationally tractable. VU is thus positioned as a proof-of-concept for AI-augmented urban analysis, outlining a path toward automated, multi-parameter identity metrics to guide adaptive urban transformation.

Transparent materials with thermal‐signature control characteristics are of paramount importance for both military and civilian applications, including camouflage, information encryption, and thermal management. However, challenges including intricate manufacturing processes and noticeable visual differences across different emissivities persist. Inspired by the amphiphilic structure of the Stenocara beetle, this work designed a binary microstructured meta‐film to control thermal signatures. Within the infrared spectrum, the binary microstructure exhibits distinct emissivities, creating thermal counterparts of “0” and “1” binary states for information encryption and thermal camouflage. In the visible range, the identical material composition of the binary microstructure leads to similar optical transparency. This renders them visually indistinguishable, thereby concealing the stored information. At the same time, the continuous metallic network embedded in the meta‐film retains excellent electric conductivity. These features enable compatibility with optical anti‐counterfeiting materials and responsiveness to external stimuli, making the proposed meta‐film a promising candidate for multispectral camouflage and multistimulus, multilevel information encryption technologies.

The glider is a civilian science vehicle for long-duration measurement of temperature, salinity and currents inside Europa's ocean; it carries oceanographic sensors only. The deposited computation script produces every number in the paper from stated inputs; among its results are hull pressure at profile floor of 59.5 megapascals, buoyancy engine energy per cycle of 432.9 kilojoules and profiles per charge of 14 profiles. The study assembles component budgets for mass and power, examines how the design behaves away from its design point, and closes with an explicit statement of what the sizing does not establish.

Background: Mine workers face elevated occupational health risks, including hypertension, work-related stress, and poor sleep quality. Non-pharmacological interventions such as music therapy offer a promising, low-cost approach to managing these conditions. Traditional Dayak Sape music, known for its soothing melodic qualities, has shown therapeutic potential in clinical settings; however, its effectiveness in occupational populations has not been studied. Methods: A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed with 52 mine workers at PT X, East Kalimantan, who had prehypertension or hypertension. Participants listened to Dayak Sape music for 10 minutes every night (Monday–Friday) over 4 weeks. Blood pressure was measured using a digital sphygmomanometer, physiological stress via salivary alpha-amylase (cocoro meter), and sleep quality using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Pre- and post-test comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results: Following the 4-week intervention, all outcome variables showed statistically significant improvements (p < 0.001). Systolic blood pressure decreased from 139 ± 14.3 to 129 ± 11.9 mmHg, and diastolic blood pressure from 93.6 ± 7.69 to 88.7 ± 5.95 mmHg. Physiological stress (salivary alpha-amylase) declined from 21.2 ± 16.0 to 9.08 ± 6.85 kU/L, and sleep quality scores improved from 7.44 ± 3.49 to 5.35 ± 2.56. Effect sizes were large to very large (r = 0.743–1.000). Conclusion: Nighttime relaxation using traditional Dayak Sape music is an effective, culturally appropriate non-pharmacological intervention for reducing blood pressure, work-related physiological stress, and improving sleep quality among mine workers. Integration of this intervention into occupational health programs in the mining sector is recommended.

documents.abstract: ABSTRACT Given the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) tools at work, understanding their health implications is critically important. We use rich survey data from Finland and apply propensity score matching that accounts for observable differences between regular AI users and non‐users to estimate the relationship between reported AI usage at work and workers’ reported stress. Regular AI use is associated with a 4.4 percentage point higher probability of reporting stress, equivalent to a 25.6% increase relative to baseline. Comparing two competing explanations, we find that this pattern is more consistent with heavier work demands than with concerns about job loss: AI use is associated with more unpaid work outside working hours and, less precisely, with intense work absorption, but not with job insecurity. Exploratory subgroup estimates are larger and individually significant for men, non‐supervisors, unionized workers and employees in medium‐sized workplaces, although the differences across subgroups are not statistically significant.

As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated in everyday decision-making, understanding how individuals respond to AI versus human advice is critical. The present study examined whether individuals are more likely to revise their initial decisions based on recommendations’ source (AI vs. Human) and stance (Agree vs. Disagree), while holding recommendation content constant. Fifty-nine participants completed eight game scenarios from popular casino games. After each initial choice, participants received a recommendation and were prompted to re-make the same decision. Mixed-effects logistic regression revealed that there is a strong tendency for participants to switch their selection when presented with disagreeing recommendations, regardless of its source. No significant differences were found in switching behaviors between AI and human-disagree conditions, though confidence increased in presence of decision switch when the opposing recommendation came from AI. Future research should explore how individual differences and contextual factors influence adoption of AI advice.
